_doc: Civil War motion data. Coordinates are [lon, lat]. Routes are drawn as smooth curves through the waypoints; marching routes are approximate (an army moved in several columns), so each campaign says so. Strengths and casualties are estimates and are shown with '≈'.

campaigns.name: Lee's invasion of Pennsylvania

waypoints.name: Williamsport, Md. (Potomac crossing; Hagerstown just north)

campaigns.strengthNote: Army of Northern Virginia at the start of the campaign: estimates run about 71,000–75,000.
campaigns.source: NPS, Gettysburg National Military Park, 'The Gettysburg Campaign'; Sears, Gettysburg (2003). Route via Culpeper, the Shenandoah Valley and Chambersburg is a simplified centre line of several corps (approximate).

campaigns.name: Lee's retreat from Gettysburg
campaigns.strengthNote: About 75,000 minus ≈23,000 Confederate casualties at Gettysburg ≈ 52,000 (rounded estimate). Using the higher ≈28,000 Confederate casualty count gives ≈47,000; and if the start strength is ≈71,000, ≈43,000–48,000. Not re-verified this session.
campaigns.source: NPS, Gettysburg NMP; Brown, Retreat from Gettysburg (2005). Route via the Fairfield road and Monterey Pass is approximate.

campaigns.name: Sherman's March to the Sea
campaigns.strengthNote: About 62,000 men left Atlanta; Union losses on the march were roughly 2,100, so ≈60,000 reached Savannah (estimate).
campaigns.source: NPS, 'Sherman's March to the Sea' (nps.gov); Official Records ser. I vol. 44. Single line through Milledgeville is a simplified centre of the two wings (approximate). Army reached the Savannah defences about Dec. 10; city occupied Dec. 21.

battles.name: Antietam
battles.outcomeNote: Tactically inconclusive; Lee withdrew to Virginia, a strategic Union success that preceded the preliminary Emancipation Proclamation.
battles.casualtiesNote: ≈23,000 killed, wounded, captured or missing (Union ≈12,400; Confederate ≈10,300). Bloodiest single day in American history.
battles.source: NPS, Antietam National Battlefield, 'Antietam Overview' (casualty figures ≈23,000).

battles.name: Gettysburg
battles.outcomeNote: Union victory; Lee's second invasion of the North ended.
battles.casualtiesNote: ≈51,000 total (Union ≈23,000; Confederate ≈23,000–28,000 by different counts). Estimate.
battles.source: NPS, Gettysburg National Military Park, 'The Battle of Gettysburg' (≈51,000 casualties).

battles.name: Savannah
battles.outcomeNote: Confederate garrison evacuated Dec. 20; Union troops occupied the city Dec. 21. Sherman offered it to Lincoln as a 'Christmas gift'.
battles.source: NPS, 'Sherman's March to the Sea'; Official Records ser. I vol. 44.

front._doc: APPROXIMATE line between Union-held and Confederate-held territory east of the Mississippi, west → east. A teaching simplification: real control was patchy (raids, guerrillas, contested border regions).
front.label: Union-held (approx.)

keys.source: Approximate: Kentucky–Tennessee line, western (West) Virginia and the Potomac front after Bull Run (McPherson, Battle Cry of Freedom, maps).

keys.label: END OF 1863
keys.source: Approximate: after Vicksburg (July 4, 1863) and Chattanooga (Nov. 1863); Rapidan line in Virginia (McPherson, Battle Cry of Freedom, maps).

keys.label: SEPTEMBER 1864
keys.source: Approximate: after the fall of Atlanta (Sept. 2, 1864) and with the siege lines at Petersburg (McPherson, Battle Cry of Freedom, maps).
